title: Altria (MO) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
transcript:
Image source: The Motley Fool.

DATE

Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026

CALL PARTICIPANTS

TAKEAWAYS

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email[email protected]

RISKS

SUMMARY

Altria Group, Inc.(MO+4.85%)reported third quarter financial results characterized by adjusted earnings growth and the continued expansion of its smoke-free portfolio. Management reported that smokeable products remains a primary contributor to earnings growth through a portfolio approach that balances premium brand leadership with discount segment options. The company noted that domestic cigarette industry volume declines moderated during the quarter, influenced by a decrease in illicit e-vapor consumption. Management highlighted significant capital returns to shareholders, including a dividend increase and an expanded share repurchase authorization. Altria also initiated legal action against the FDA to establish a more predictable product authorization process and address the growth of the illicit market.

Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator:Good day, and welcome to the Altria Group 2026 Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call. Today's call is scheduled to last about 1 hour, including remarks by Altria's management and a question-and-answer session. Representatives of the investment community and media on the call will be able to ask questions following the conclusion of the prepared remarks. I would now like to turn the call over to Mac Livingston, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead, sir.

Mac Livingston:Thanks, Olivia. Good morning, and thank you for joining us. This morning, Sal Mancuso, Altria's CEO, and Heather Newman, our CFO, will discuss Altria's 2026 third quarter and first 9 months business results. Earlier today, we issued a press release providing our results. The release, presentation and quarterly metrics are all available at altria.com. During our call today, unless otherwise stated, we're comparing results to the same period in 2025. Our remarks contain forward-looking statements, including projections of future results. Please review the forward-looking and cautionary statements section at the end of today's earnings release for various factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from projections.

Future dividend payments and share repurchases remain subject to the discretion of our Board of Directors. We report our financial results in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles. Today's call will contain various operating results on both a reported and adjusted basis. Adjusted results exclude special items that affect comparisons with reported results. Descriptions of these non-GAAP financial measures and reconciliations to the most comparable GAAP financial measures are included in today's earnings release and on our website at altria.com. Finally, all references in today's remarks to nicotine consumers or consumers within a specific nicotine category or segment refer to existing adult nicotine consumers 21 years of age or older. With that, I'll turn the call over to Sal.

Salvatore Mancuso:Thanks, Mac. Good morning, and thank you for joining us. Altria delivered strong financial performance in the third quarter, growing adjusted diluted earnings per share by 4.8%, while continuing to invest in our vision and building on our foundation for the future. In smokeable products, PM USA grew operating companies income through its data-driven total portfolio approach with Cowboy Cut strengthening Marlboro's premium position and Basic continuing to gain share in discount. In smoke-free, Helix made meaningful progress by expanding on! PLUS 12-milligram nationwide, investing in brand-building initiatives and preparing for its next wave of innovation, which is now underway with the introduction of Blueberry Mint and Mango Pineapple flavor extensions at retail.

Our highly cash-generative businesses supported significant returns to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases, while we continue to invest in support of our vision. In August, we announced our 61st dividend increase in 57 years, and our Board recently authorized a $1 billion expansion of our existing share repurchase program. Our strong performance through the first 9 months and confidence in our full year plan allowed us to raise our earnings guidance for the year. My remarks this morning will focus on third quarter performance from on! and the evolving regulatory environment. I'll then turn it over to Heather, who will provide further details on our business results and 2026 financial outlook.

Let's begin with the nicotine pouch category in our growing on! portfolio. Nicotine pouches continue to drive volume growth in the oral tobacco category, which we estimate increased 5.5% over the past 6 months. In the third quarter, the nicotine pouch category grew 5.8 share points and now represents more than 60% of the total oral category. As the category continues to expand, Helix is delivering solid results and strengthening on!'s position in an increasingly competitive marketplace. In the third quarter, on! reported shipment volume increased 13.3% to 47.8 million cans. Year-to-date, reported shipment volume increased 7.7%. On! retail share was 8.3% in the third quarter, up 0.1 versus the prior year and down 0.3 sequentially.

This performance is encouraging as on!'s retail price continued to move higher and competitive investment remained elevated across the category during the quarter. Higher nicotine strengths and broader flavor variety continued to drive growth in the nicotine pouch category, and Helix is expanding on! PLUS to better meet this consumer demand. In the third quarter, Helix expanded on! PLUS 12-milligram nationally across mint, wintergreen and tobacco. And this month, introduced Blueberry Mint and Mango Pineapple, and we're excited to announce that Watermelon Mint will join the portfolio in select retail locations in November with plans for more flavor innovation to come. We believe these additions strengthen the on! PLUS portfolio and are supporting it with superior retail execution.

Earlier this year, Helix launched a retail trade program that secured premium positioning in stores representing approximately 90% of its volume. In an increasingly competitive category, we believe this positioning provides valuable visibility to support awareness, trial and conversion. Beyond retail, Helix continues to invest in building the on! brand and creating distinctive consumer experiences. Earlier this month, Helix hosted the inaugural on!vitational, an invite-only golf tournament in Palm Beach, Florida. The event gave on! consumers a chance to compete alongside athletes and golf personalities. Helix highlighted the tournament with digital content designed to extend its adult nicotine consumer reach beyond the event itself.

Planned as a multiyear platform, we believe the on!vitational can become a signature brand experience that builds lasting equity and further differentiates on! over time. These efforts are grounded in responsibility with safeguards to limit reach to underage audiences and a strong focus on regulatory compliance. We're encouraged by the progress Helix has made so far this year and the foundation it is building for future growth. With a broader on! PLUS portfolio, premium retail visibility and growing brand equity, we continue to believe on! is well positioned to compete and drive long-term profitable growth in the category. From a regulatory perspective, the FDA's enforcement guidance allowed Helix to move through the regulatory process more efficiently. However, guidance can change.

Sustained progress on harm reduction requires a more durable foundation, an efficient and predictable authorization process established through rulemaking. That's why Helix and NJOY brought legal action against the FDA during the quarter. The complaint asked the court to require the FDA to establish a review process that meets the 180-day time frame set by Congress and to allow our products with applications pending beyond that time frame to be in market while the agency puts a new process in place. Following the filing, the FDA announced plans to evaluate changes to the PMTA framework.

The agency acknowledged challenges it has faced implementing the 2021 PMTA rule, including the widespread growth of the illicit market and slow pace of new product authorizations, and intends to pursue new rulemaking. We welcome this development and believe the modernized framework that maintains a high bar with rigorous standards for new products and provides greater clarity, predictability and efficiency is critical to advancing the long-term harm reduction opportunity. A more efficient authorization process must be paired with consistent illicit product enforcement. On that front, we continue to see encouraging progress on illicit e-vapor enforcement as federal, state and local policymakers and law enforcement take meaningful steps to close gaps and hold bad actors accountable across the supply chain.

These enforcement efforts appear to be impacting e-vapor category dynamics. At the end of September, we estimate there were approximately 20 million adult vapers, down 1 million versus a year ago, primarily driven by fewer e-vapor consumers using illicit products. Ultimately, we believe sustained enforcement and a more efficient authorization process are both necessary to establish a level-playing field for legal manufacturers and expand access to high-quality smoke-free products for adult nicotine consumers. We remain confident in the opportunities in front of us. The breadth of our portfolio, the passion of our talented employees, our manufacturing capabilities and the financial flexibility supported by PM USA's import-export activity position us to deliver strong shareholder returns while investing for the future.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Heather to provide additional details on our business and financial results.

Heather Newman:Thanks, Sal, and good morning, everyone. Altria's operating companies effectively executed their strategies and delivered impressive third quarter and first 9 months financial performance. Adjusted diluted earnings per share increased 4.8% in the third quarter and by 5.1% for the first 9 months. We delivered these results in an environment of continued economic pressure on adult smokers. The overall cost of goods and services has risen roughly 30% since 2021, putting sustained pressure on household budgets, while more recent increases in gas prices have further constrained discretionary income. Against this backdrop, the smokeable products segment remains a key contributor to earnings growth.

Our smokeable strategy is to maximize profitability over the long term, while balancing investments in Marlboro and funding the growth of smoke-free products. PM USA's portfolio approach supports this strategy by offering options across brands and price points, while driving strong financial results. Adjusted operating companies income grew by 3.9% to $3.1 billion in the third quarter and by 4.1% to $8.8 billion for the first 9 months. Adjusted OCI margins expanded to 64.5% for the third quarter and 64.8% for the first 9 months, up 0.1 percentage points and 0.4 percentage points, respectively. Price realization was 4.4% for the quarter, reflecting the mix impact of both Marlboro Cowboy Cut and Basic volume growth. Smokeable volume declines remained moderate.

Reported domestic cigarette volumes declined by 2.9% in the third quarter and 2.8% for the first 9 months. When adjusted for trade inventory movements, we estimate domestic cigarette volumes for the third quarter and for the first 9 months declined by 4%, slightly below an estimated 5% decline for the industry. Within the highly profitable premium segment, Marlboro strengthened its long-standing leadership position. The introduction of Cowboy Cut provided price-sensitive Marlboro smokers with a premium option in a challenging economic environment, contributing to Marlboro's share performance in the third quarter. Marlboro expanded its share of the premium segment to 60%, up 0.3 versus the prior year and 0.4 sequentially.

Marlboro's overall retail share was unchanged sequentially and down 1 share point versus the year ago period as economic pressures continue to drive discount segment growth. In the third quarter, discount retail share grew by 2 share points and is now 34.1% of the category. Basic continues to support PM USA's RGM strategy by providing a competitive offering in stores where discount brands are most relevant. During the quarter, Basic's retail share expanded by 0.3 sequentially and 1.8 share points year-over-year. The combined performance of Marlboro and Basic reflects the effectiveness of PM USA's total portfolio approach. Total PM USA retail share expanded 0.2 share point sequentially and 0.3 versus a year ago.

In cigars, for the third quarter and first 9 months, reported shipment volume increased 0.9% and 2%, respectively, as Middleton continued to significantly outperform in a declining large mass cigar industry. Let's now turn to the oral tobacco products segment. Financial results reflect continued investment behind on! PLUS and the impact of lower MST volumes. Adjusted OCI decreased by 3.7% to $443 million in the third quarter and by 4% to $1.3 billion for the first 9 months. Adjusted OCI margins remained strong at 66.4% for the third quarter and 66.8% for the first 9 months.

Total segment reported shipment volumes decreased 4.3% for the third quarter and 5.4% for the first 9 months as growth in on! was more than offset by the lower MST volumes. When adjusted for trade inventory movements, we estimate third quarter and first 9 months oral tobacco products segment volumes both declined by an estimated 5%. Oral tobacco products segment retail share was 27.9% for the third quarter and 28.6% for the first 9 months. In the highly profitable moist smokeless tobacco segment, Copenhagen maintained its long-standing premium leadership. Turning to ABI's financial results. We recorded $191 million of adjusted equity earnings in the third quarter, up 21.7% versus the prior year.

We continue to view our ABI stake as a financial investment, and our goal remains to maximize the long-term value of the investment for our shareholders. Our strong financial performance for the first 9 months enabled us to return over $6 billion to our shareholders, including $5.3 billion in dividends and $735 million in share repurchases. We remain committed to providing significant cash returns to our shareholders as demonstrated by our recent dividend increase. In August, our Board increased our quarterly dividend by 4.7% to $1.11 per share, our 61st increase in 57 years and consistent with our progressive dividend goal of mid-single-digit annual growth.

And today, we announced that our Board authorized a $1 billion expansion of our existing share repurchase program, which now expires on December 31, 2027. In addition, our balance sheet remains strong. Our debt-to-EBITDA ratio as of September 30 was 1.9x, in line with our target of approximately 2x. Finally, let's turn to our financial outlook. Our businesses performed extremely well in a dynamic environment during the first 9 months of the year, and we maintained the strength of our core tobacco businesses while investing towards our vision.

As a result, we raised our earnings guidance and now expect to deliver adjusted diluted EPS in a range of $5.66 to $5.74, representing a growth rate of 4.5% to 6% from a base of $5.42 in 2025. With that, we'll wrap up, and Sal and I will be happy to take your questions. While the calls are being compiled, I'll remind you that today's earnings release and our non-GAAP reconciliations are available on altria.com. We've also posted our quarterly metrics, which include pricing, inventory and other items. Operator, let's open the question-and-answer period.

Operator:[Operator Instructions]. The first question is from Faham Baig at UBS.

Mirza Faham Baig:A couple of questions from me, please. Firstly, on industry cigarette volumes and then on Marlboro Cowboy Cut. So on the industry, the volumes have remained pretty resilient this year, and it looks like the sequential growth in the discount segment moderated somewhat this quarter despite the higher gasoline prices. Are there any particular factors you would call out behind the resilience? And more broadly, are you seeing any evidence that the pressure on the smoker is beginning to ease? And then secondly, on Cowboy Cut, can you maybe help us understand where you see the sub-brand's positioning within the broader Marlboro portfolio?

I know, initially, it was launched at a discount to Marlboro Black, but we're now seeing it priced above Black in some states, while in other states, it's sort of yet to be introduced. How should we think about the positioning and the intended role of Cowboy Cut longer term?

Salvatore Mancuso:Yes, terrific. And thanks for your questions. Two really good questions. So let's start with the industry volume. The consumer continues to be under economic pressure, no doubt. The inflation, which has been in place for multiple years, continues to put pressure on their everyday goods. I would say, though, that nicotine, historically, has been a little bit more resilient than other CPG categories, for sure. But when you look at the moderation of the decline rates that you're seeing in the cigarette category, that's primarily being driven by the lower-cost category movement from the illicit e-vapor category. And I would say, probably, 2 factors are driving that.

One is these products have been in the market for multiple years now. So consumers that were interested in it have moved. And then the second factor is, as we talked about earlier, the focus on enforcement for illicit products, we think that is having some impact. Now we need that -- those efforts to be sustained and to continue, but it's definitely having an impact on supply chain in our minds. As far as Cowboy Cut, let's start with the smokeable strategy, which is to maximize profitability over the long term and balance investments in Marlboro with investments in our long-term vision.

Cowboy Cut provides a premium Marlboro option at the right price to retain value-sensitive smokers within that franchise. It delivers a classic Marlboro experience and is supported by brand equity that draws on its American heritage and complements the nation's 250th celebration. It's pretty widely distributed. It's in about 100,000 stores, which is about 75% of the cigarette volume. And it's a strategy we've deployed before. You've seen it with Marlboro Special Select. You've seen it with Marlboro Black, where you have introductory pricing and then you will see PM USA take pricing or margin up those SKUs over time. Obviously, you talked about different states and different pricing.

Well, that's reflective of the data analytics and RGM tools that PM USA has been able to deploy. So we're really, really pleased with the impact on Marlboro. You saw Marlboro share of the premium has reached about 60%. It's up 0.3 year-over-year. So we feel really good about the overall performance of our smokeable segment and the cigarette category in particular.

Operator:The next question is from Matt Smith at Stifel.

Matthew Smith:Just wanted to come back to the raise of the full year guidance for EPS. Can you talk about where you're seeing strength relative to your previous expectations? And have you stepped up your investment levels behind some of the initiatives, whether it's behind the smoke-free vision investments or in combustible and leaned into the volume opportunity that becomes the future pricing opportunity over time?

Heather Newman:Yes. Thanks for the question. Just as a reminder, in the beginning of the year, we did have our guidance range, 2.5% to 5%. And as we performed really strongly through the first 9 months, it's given us confidence to not only narrow, but raise the guidance to the 4.5% to 6%. I will say that's inclusive of investments that we tend to invest in our smoke-free vision really around on! PLUS and you're starting to see that play out in the marketplace with the 12-milligram product as well as our flavor line extensions. The other thing that we're mindful of is that we continue to be challenged by a pretty difficult macroeconomic environment for the consumer.

We feel great about our RGM capabilities to manage through that environment as they remain under pressure. Gas prices are still elevated. Sal's already talked about inflation. But this new guidance range of the 4.5% to 6%, we feel really confident that we can deliver throughout the rest of the year.

Matthew Smith:Appreciate that, Heather. And a follow-up on the quarter. Duty drawback, I think it was $124 million revenue benefit. Previously, you talked about it being pretty equally phased in the second half of the year. Does that -- is the third quarter level a reasonable amount for the fourth quarter? I know there's some catch-up timing in there. I'll pass it on after that.

Heather Newman:Yes. I appreciate it. Our expectations have not changed. We did have some slight benefit in Q2 from the timing of the FET credit that we benefited from in Q3, but our expectations for the second half of the year in terms of stepping up and the imbalance between the quarters have not changed.

Operator:The next question is from Bonnie Herzog at Goldman Sachs.

Bonnie Herzog:I had a quick follow-up on what you just touched on, Heather. In terms of the double duty drawback benefit, you did export 10% of your cig volume in Q3. So I guess I was hoping to hear a little more color on how we should think about your ability to ramp this further next year, especially given your contract manufacturing agreement with Philip Morris will kick in. So if you could talk about that also, that would be appreciated.

Heather Newman:Yes. Thank you, Bonnie. So in the first half of the year, we were really establishing the contract manufacturing arrangements, and then we communicated that step-up balanced approach through the second half of the year without getting too far ahead in terms of expectations for 2027. You are right to call out that, that PMI agreement does not start until 2027. And so that benefit will certainly kick in. What we're working against and where you see the increase from Q2 to Q3 is our current CMA arrangements. And again, without getting too far ahead, we expect to be pretty balanced across Q3 and Q4 here.

Bonnie Herzog:Okay. And then maybe if I could just switch gears a bit, and I have a question on vapor, which you touched on. But just in terms of NJOY ACE, I believe you've addressed the patent infringement issues and you're able to bring the product back to the market. So curious if you're planning on doing this maybe soon. And how you're thinking about what role vapor can ultimately play in your smoke-free portfolio? And then if or when you bring it back to the market? I guess I'm trying to understand how you're going to manage it.

I mean, would you manage it differently or run the business differently than what you had done before because I'm thinking about the substantial operating losses you used to have on the brand.

Salvatore Mancuso:So you are correct to point out that we have worked around the patent issues that forced us to pull NJOY ACE out of the market. We have not announced when we're going back in the market, but we do plan on being back in the e-vapor market. You're also right to point out that our approach is going to be, I would say, I would characterize it as very disciplined. The market, while we've seen some improvement, is still predominantly driven by the illicit category. And we want to compete in the market, but we want to do it in a disciplined way and in a profitable way over time.

So for us, we continue to engage with stakeholders to drive enforcement activity to maintain or sustain it over time. We also recognize that it's important for the FDA to authorize products more quickly. We also recognize that there are certain attributes related to the illicit category that appeal to consumers. So if you think about our innovative pipeline, we want to delight the consumer over time. So we continue to innovate further on NJOY ACE. But our approach will be disciplined, and we'll have more to say as time proceeds.

Operator:The next question is from Andrei Andon at Jefferies.

Andrei Andon-Ionita:Two from me, please. Firstly, following up to Bonnie's question on vapes. We've already seen a legal competitor launch flavored vapes in August, September this year. Where do you see such product legal flavored vapes potentially gaining share? Are they more likely to be a pressure point on cigarettes or rather on illicit vapes? And then secondly, it's encouraging to see on! grow year-on-year in Q3, but I believe the volumes have still declined relative to the previous quarter to Q2 '26. What are your expectations for volume growth for on! into next quarter and into next year? And what would underpin this?

Salvatore Mancuso:Yes. So let me start with your vapor question, and it's a good one. Look, e-vapor is a far lower risk proposition for smokers and exposes those smokers to lower levels of smoking. So we believe e-vapor continues to play an important role in long-term harm reduction. We also recognize that flavors is something that attracts smokers to a less harmful product. So we do think it plays a role. But as we said, the category itself is upside down. The risk of consumers using illicit vapors, which have not been through the regulatory process, threatens the long-term tobacco harm reduction opportunity.

And so we continue to engage with our stakeholders, as I said earlier, to drive the illicit enforcement, and we have seen definitely a stepped-up level of enforcement. So over the long term, we believe vapor does play an important role, and we will participate in that. Your question on growth of the nicotine pouch. Look, the volume decline you're seeing is primarily driven actually by the MST category as consumers move from MST into the nicotine pouch category. We're really excited about on! PLUS. We believe that the NICOSILK technology for the pouch is a differentiator. But we also recognize that higher levels of nicotine and flavors drive a lot of the consumer growth.

So we're excited that we've got 12 milligrams just went into the market recently. We haven't really seen the impact of that on retail share yet. And then, we are entering the retail space with flavors, Mango Pineapple and Blueberry Mint. We announced Watermelon Mint coming in November in select stores. And we plan on having future innovation through flavor deliveries in the future. So we're excited about the pipeline. We're excited about the tobacco harm reduction opportunity that nicotine pouch provides the adult nicotine consumers. So we look forward to on! PLUS and on! classic continuing to play a role in that.

Operator:[Operator Instructions]. The next question is from Pallav Mittal at Barclays.

Pallav Mittal:So just to follow up on volumes. See, volumes are up 13% Y-o-Y in the third quarter. But when I look at scanner data, it is down mid-teens or something like that. So is there a significant inventory as you roll out 12 mg or is it something else?

Salvatore Mancuso:I wouldn't say significant, but I would say there's obviously some pipeline inventory as we launched the 12-milligram across mint, wintergreen and tobacco. And then you've got the flavor introductions that we talked about earlier. There are some differences on how you read scanner data where they look at pouches versus cans. So there's a little bit of noise in that, but nothing significant. But within a quarter, you're going to have some pipeline movement, not just for us, you have other brands introducing new SKUs as well. So I think you got to look at that over a longer period of time.

Pallav Mittal:Sure. And if I can then ask on your cigarette business, okay? And if I exclude the double duty drawback for a moment, then the EBIT on your core cigarette business is flat despite cigarette volumes being much better than what anyone of us would have thought at the start of the year. So how should we think about that? And how do you plan to grow your cigarette profits, especially as cigarette volumes start lapping tougher comps over the next few months?

Salvatore Mancuso:Yes. I think it's, frankly, a little unfair to pick out one aspect of the margin and pull it out and say, "Well, EBIT is flat," or -- you got to look across the entire composition of the margin, which is driven by pricing, cost management. Duty drawback is part of it. We feel really good about our ability to grow income within the cigarette category. We had strong OCI performance through the first 9 months. You've seen Marlboro perform really well in the highly profitable premium segment. PM USA's overall share has grown through the total portfolio approach. And -- so we feel really good about the smokeable segment in general.

And as Heather stated earlier, that confidence in that performance through the first 9 months allowed us to raise guidance, and we were happy to provide that as well. So we feel really good about the business overall. But thanks for the question.

Pallav Mittal:Sure. And if I can just squeeze one more in on duty drawback. You are exiting the year at around $500 million annual benefit from duty drawback based on the current run rate. And then as I think about next year, you will probably ramp up the current program and then the PM contract agreement will also kick in. So can you give us a broad range? I mean, from $500 million, can it go to $1 billion? Or are we looking at something around $700 million, $800 million for next year?

Salvatore Mancuso:No, we're not providing that range. I understand the question. I'll remind you, as Heather said earlier, you are not seeing the impact of the contract manufacturing agreement with PMI, yet that will happen next year. So we talked about that this volume does build over time. I think Heather laid it out really well in earlier questions and in her remarks. So -- but we won't provide any further guidance on that.

Operator:And the final question is from Eric Serotta at Morgan Stanley.

Eric Serotta:A couple of things. First, Sal, can I get your perspective a little bit in terms of nicotine pouch category growth over the shorter term and then over the mid- to long term, seen an incredible amount of innovation from both Altria Helix and your competitors over the past 4, 5 months as the regulatory environment has changed. At the same time, the category growth rate hasn't really materially accelerated. Coming up, you're going to have the leader in the category, effectively lowering the price per pouch. How do you see this all playing out in terms of category volume and revenue growth over the short term?

And then any change to your thinking about how big this category can be over the mid- to long term?

Salvatore Mancuso:Yes. Look, it's a really good question. The nicotine pouch category has seen tremendous growth, much of it driven by MST consumers that move into nicotine pouch. There are a number of reasons for that, including social friction. If you think about -- there's no spitting, as an example, with nicotine pouch. You've also seen some growth from cigarette consumers that are seeking a reduced harm way of enjoying nicotine, if you will. The rate of acceleration, look, as the numbers get bigger, like any category, you would see that the percentage change might not be as high as when you're first seeing the adoption, obviously. So that's something to consider, right?

But we see the category as a tremendous tobacco harm reduction opportunity. It's still predominantly male. I think if you look overseas, you have seen women and other demographics adopt the product. So we think that continues to be an opportunity. And you're right to point out, it is a highly competitive category. It's a growing category. So you're going to see competition, and we're used to that. I mean the cigarette category has been highly competitive. The smokeless category was highly competitive. But we believe over the long term, tobacco-like margins are very achievable in this category. We see on! and on! PLUS is a premium proposition. We continue to invest in the pipeline of innovation.

We continue to invest in the brand. We were really excited to see the on!vitational take place. So we feel really good about the category and the potential it has for long-term harm reduction in the U.S. market.

Eric Serotta:Great. And then a quick follow-up. Just turning to your slide on the industry volume decomposition for cigarettes. The price elasticity impact ticked down about 20 basis points over the past quarter. What do you think is driving that? And then additionally, the macro cross-category and other continues to tick lower. I know you called out cross-category at less than 50 basis points versus about 50 basis points. So maybe there's just some rounding here. But just wondering what's driving the reductions on both of those lines.

Salvatore Mancuso:Yes. The cigarette price-elasticity coefficient hasn't changed. It's still negative 0.35. So the impact you're seeing is just a year-over-year price change across the category, if you will, and it's just multiplication. As far as the macro and cross-category movement, it's really the cross-category movement and the moderation of that, that is lowering that number over time. Macroeconomics still continue to be headwinds, if you will, for the consumer. It continues to put pressure on consumer spending. Obviously, we're paying very close attention to that. But as Heather pointed out earlier, our ability to use data analytics and RGM tools, I think, positions us really well to navigate through that.

So PM USA and the employees there as well as Helix and UST continue to use these tools very effectively, and we feel good about our ability to continue to manage through that.

Operator:There appears to be no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Mac Livingston for any closing remarks.

Mac Livingston:Thanks to everyone for joining us today. If you have further questions, please feel free to reach out to the IR team. Thanks.

Operator:This concludes today's call. Thank you for your participation. You may disconnect at any time.
